title: Completed algebraic closure over a complete stable field
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], complete for a nontrivial real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value, and stable [def-trf-stable-nonarchimedean-field]. Choose an algebraic closure $k^a/k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] with its spectral absolute value, and let $k'$ be its metric completion, with the extending absolute value. Then $k'$ is an algebraically closed complete field extending $k$ isometrically. Every finite-dimensional $k$-linear subspace $V\subset k'$ has an orthogonal $k$-basis for the restricted absolute value: $|\sum_i a_iv_i|=\max_i|a_i||v_i|$ for all $a_i\in k$. The zero subspace has the empty basis. No spherical completeness or discreteness of the valuation is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.1/3 and Corollary 2.4.3/10; their application in Section 5.3.4, opening paragraph and Lemma 1 proof, printed pp.218–219 (scan PDF pp.224–225). Primary scan read online 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-spectral-norm-algebraic-extension], the spectral norm on $k^a$ is a multiplicative nonarchimedean norm restricting to that of $k$. By [lem-sfb-normed-field-completion], its completion $k'$ is a complete normed field and $k^a\to k'$ is an isometric field inclusion. The image of $k^a$ is dense by the definition of metric completion. For $x,y\in k'$, choose sequences $x_j,y_j\in k^a$ converging to them. Taking limits in $|x_j+y_j|\le\max(|x_j|,|y_j|)$ proves the same inequality in $k'$. The composite $k\to k^a\to k'$ is isometric, so its absolute value is nontrivial.

source.place: Sections 3.2.4 and 3.4.1: extending the spectral valuation and taking the metric completion.

proof.text: Let $f\in k'[T]$ be monic of degree $n\ge1$. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $k'$ using [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Equip it with the extending multiplicative nonarchimedean spectral norm by [lem-trf-spectral-norm-algebraic-extension], applied over the complete nontrivially valued field $k'$. Choose a root $a\in\Omega$ of $f$ and set $M=\max(|a|,1)$. For any real $r>0$, put $\varepsilon=(r/M)^n/(n+1)>0$. Apply [lem-sfb-monic-dense-approximation] to the dense subfield $k^a\subset k'$: there is a monic $g\in k^a[T]$ of degree $n$ whose coefficientwise image $h\in k'[T]$ satisfies $|h_i-f_i|<\varepsilon$ for every $i$.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.1/3, proof, printed pp.146–147 (PDF pp.154–155): approximate the finitely many coefficients in the dense algebraically closed subfield.

proof.text: Since $k^a$ is algebraically closed, [lem-weil-alg-closed-linear-factorization] factors $g$ into $n$ linear factors with roots $c_j\in k^a$. The same factorization makes $h$ split over $\Omega$. Thus [lem-sfb-roots-coefficient-proximity], applied to $\Omega/k'$ with its extending norm, gives $b\in\Omega$ with $h(b)=0$ and $|a-b|<((n+1)\varepsilon)^{1/n}M=r$. Evaluating the factorization gives $\prod_j(b-c_j)=0$. A finite product in a field is zero only if a factor is zero, so $b=c_j\in k^a\subset k'$. Therefore every positive-radius ball about $a$ meets $k'$.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.1/3, proof, printed p.147 (PDF p.155): approximate roots; the quantitative root bound is the cited Mathlib input and works also in positive characteristic.

proof.text: The image of $k'$ in $\Omega$ is a one-dimensional $k'$-linear subspace. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-dimensional-subspace-closed] with scalar field $k'$ and ambient vector space $\Omega$. Its scalar field is complete and nontrivially valued by step 1. The norm metric on $\Omega$ is Hausdorff, and its vector-space operations are continuous: addition satisfies $|(x+y)-(x_0+y_0)|\le\max(|x-x_0|,|y-y_0|)$, negation is an isometry, and $|cx-dy|\le\max(|c||x-y|,|c-d||y|)$ with $|c|\le\max(|d|,|c-d|)$ locally bounded. The inclusion is isometric by step 2. Thus $k'$ is closed in $\Omega$. Step 3 puts $a$ in its closure, hence $a\in k'$. Every monic polynomial of positive degree over $k'$ has a root in $k'$; dividing a nonconstant polynomial by its nonzero leading coefficient reduces to this case. This is algebraic closedness as in [def-weil-algebraic-closure].

source.place: Proposition 3.4.1/3, proof, printed p.147 (PDF p.155): the approximate roots have limit in the complete subfield; closedness states this without choosing a subsequence.

proof.text: Every finite-dimensional $k$-linear subspace $U\subset k^a$ has an orthogonal basis. Indeed, choose a finite $k$-basis $u_1,\ldots,u_d$ of $U$. These elements are algebraic over $k$, so [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension] shows that $E=k(u_1,\ldots,u_d)$ is finite over $k$. The restricted norm on $E$ is its minimal-polynomial spectral norm: for an element of $E$, the monic polynomial of least degree over $k$ is unchanged by embedding $E\subset k^a$, since evaluation vanishes before the embedding exactly when it vanishes after it. Stability [def-trf-stable-nonarchimedean-field] therefore gives a finite orthogonal $k$-basis of $E$. Applying [lem-trf-cartesian-subspace] to $U\subset E$ gives the desired orthogonal basis. For $U=0$ take the empty basis.

source.place: Corollary 2.4.3/10 as used in Lemma 5.3.4/1, printed p.219 (PDF p.225): first verify that the algebraic closure is k-cartesian using stability and Proposition 2.4.1/5.

proof.text: Let $V\subset k'$ have positive finite dimension $d$. By [lem-trf-finite-ultrametric-almost-orthogonal-basis] with $r=1/2$, choose a basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ with $|\sum_i a_i e_i|\ge\tfrac12\max_i|a_i||e_i|$. Set $\alpha=\tfrac12\min_i|e_i|>0$. Then $|\sum_i a_i e_i|\ge\alpha\max_i|a_i|$ for all coefficients. Density of $k^a$ gives $w_i\in k^a$ with $|w_i-e_i|<\alpha$ for every $i$. This uses completeness only of the scalar field $k$, exactly as required in the almost-orthogonal-basis lemma.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.3/7, printed p.101 (PDF p.109): the lower coordinate bound and approximation of the finitely many basis vectors; weak cartesianness is supplied by the cited almost-orthogonal basis.

proof.text: For coefficients not all zero put $A=\max_i|a_i|>0$, $x=\sum_i a_i e_i$ and $y=\sum_i a_i w_i$. The finite ultrametric sum inequality gives $|y-x|\le\max_i|a_i||w_i-e_i|<\alpha A\le|x|$. The inequalities $|y|\le\max(|x|,|y-x|)$ and $|x|\le\max(|y|,|y-x|)$ force $|y|=|x|$. This equality also holds when all coefficients vanish. Thus the assignment $e_i\mapsto w_i$ defines a linear isometry $T:V\to U=\sum_i kw_i\subset k^a$: it is well-defined on basis coordinates; the norm equality makes it injective; and the definition of $U$ makes it surjective.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.3/7, proof, printed p.101 (PDF p.109): explicit strict ultrametric perturbation calculation.

proof.text: Apply step 5 to $U$ and let $v_1,\ldots,v_d$ be its orthogonal basis. Then $T^{-1}v_i$ is a basis of $V$, and the isometry gives $|\sum_i a_iT^{-1}v_i|=|\sum_i a_iv_i|=\max_i|a_i||v_i|=\max_i|a_i||T^{-1}v_i|$. When $V=0$ its empty basis has sum and maximum both zero. This proves every asserted orthogonality clause without discreteness or spherical completeness.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.3/7 and Corollary 2.4.3/10, printed pp.101–102 (PDF pp.109–110); transfer across the explicit isometry.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-O1-8226f7c90 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all 8 steps and every cited statement. The statement is unchanged and correct. Step 1: the spectral norm on k^a (lem-trf-spectral-norm-algebraic-extension, F=k) and normed-field completion give a complete, ultrametric, nontrivial k' containing k isometrically. Steps 2-3: monic dense approximation (D=k^a dense in k') and root proximity in Ω/k' (h splits via the linear factorization in k^a) give a root b with |a-b|<r, since ((n+1)ε)^{1/n}M=r. Then ∏(b-c_j)=0 puts b in k^a; this uses no separability and no characteristic assumption. Step 4: the finite-dimensional-subspace-closed lemma with E=k' complete and nontrivial makes k' closed in Ω, so k' is algebraically closed. Step 5: the restriction of the k^a spectral norm to E=k(u_i) equals s_{E/k}. Both depend only on the minimal polynomial over k, and the formula max|a_i|^{1/i} matches sup|p_j|^{1/(d-j)}. Stability and lem-trf-cartesian-subspace then give an orthogonal basis of U. Step 6: the almost-orthogonal lemma over complete k with r=1/2 gives α=½min|e_i|>0, and density gives the w_i. Step 7 is elementary (BGR 2.4.3/7): the error bound is strict because the max is finite and A>0, so |y|=|x| and T is a linear isometry onto the span of the w_i. Step 8 moves the basis back through T^{-1}. proof_deps equal the union of the steps' uses, and there is no cycle. The off-unit inputs are all mathlib leaves, so no tool_uses are needed. No SGA. Edge cases checked: V=0, k already algebraically closed, Q_p→C_p, char p and inseparable f. BGR is not in local literature (WANTED). Advisory: the existing lem-trf-sepclosed-rank-one-completion and lem-sfb-dense-subfield-algebraic-root-approximation could replace steps 2-4. The delivery creates no new nodes, so it adds no duplicates. No changes.

lean.statement: theorem completedAlgebraicClosure_cartesian (K : Type u) [NontriviallyNormedField K] [IsUltrametricDist K] [CompleteSpace K] (hK : IsStableNonarchimedeanField K) (L : Type v) [NormedField L] [NormedAlgebra K L] [IsAlgClosure K L] : IsAlgClosed (UniformSpace.Completion L) ∧ CompleteSpace (UniformSpace.Completion L) ∧ IsUltrametricDist (UniformSpace.Completion L) ∧ Isometry (algebraMap K (UniformSpace.Completion L)) ∧ ∀ (V : Submodule K (UniformSpace.Completion L)) [FiniteDimensional K V], ∃ b : Module.Basis (Fin (Module.finrank K V)) K V, ∀ a : Fin (Module.finrank K V) → K, ‖∑ i, a i • b i‖₊ = Finset.univ.sup (fun i ↦ ‖a i‖₊ * ‖b i‖₊)
